lines.trans: You know, Lev, I gain weight very quickly.
Do not say that, you look wonderful!
And who will love me if I get fat?
People love a person not for their figure.
They love you simply for your kind heart.
Do you truly think so sincerely?
Yes, I am speaking the pure truth.
Then serve me a couple more pancakes!
There, that is much better, eat up!
Thank you very much for the delicious pancakes.
Call me simply Lev from now on.

examples.text: Тогда положите мне ещё парочку блинов!
examples.trans: Then serve me a couple more pancakes!

examples.text: Большое спасибо вам за вкусные блины.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('big, large').

examples.text: Аракелян просит время. Сумма очень большая.
examples.trans: Arakelyan is asking for more time. The sum is very large.

meanings.note: the comparative 'быстрее', often as an order
the comparative 'быстрее', often as an order

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('tasty, delicious').

examples.trans: The bread rings are very tasty.

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, присядьте. Попробуйте чай с сушками, очень вкусные.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, have a seat. Try the tea with bread rings, they're very tasty.
All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'глядеть'). Used as an verbal verb meaning 'to look, appear'.

examples.trans: On top the costume looks simply super!

examples.text: Не говорите так, вы прекрасно выглядите!
examples.trans: Do not say that, you look wonderful!

говорить.gloss: to speak, to say, to talk

meanings.note: Я тебе говорю = I'm telling you
emphatic at the start of a sentence
много дел = a lot to do

examples.trans: I have a lot to do.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: in greetings: добрый день, добрый вечер

examples.text: Добрый вечер, Вика. С Новым годом!
examples.trans: Good evening, Vika. Happy New Year!

meanings.en: to agree, to come to an arrangement

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('other, another, different').

examples.text: Послушайте, а можно в другое место? Здесь плохо пахнет.
examples.trans: Listen, could we go somewhere else? It smells bad in here.

meanings.note: думать о + prepositional = to think about

examples.trans: I have no time to think about that.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: condition: если хочешь = if you want; а если нет? = and if not?
in threats: ты ещё увидишь = you'll see

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'ис-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'кренне').

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, я вам искренне сочувствую.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, I sincerely sympathize with you.

examples.text: Я вам искренне сочувствую, но мне пора работать.
examples.trans: I sincerely feel for you, but it is time for me to work.
Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

meanings.note: used when speaking to or about children

examples.trans: Eat well so that you grow up strong.
There, that is much better, eat up!

examples.text: Настя, почему ты не кушаешь мясо?
examples.trans: Nastya, why do you not eat meat?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to love, to like', paired with 'полюбить'.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.
Call me simply Lev from now on.

examples.text: А вы называйте меня просто Вика.
examples.trans: And you call me simply Vika.

examples.text: Они называют себя лучшим рестораном города.
examples.trans: They call themselves the best restaurant in town.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
middle name derived from father's name

examples.trans: Agreed, simply Lev, without a patronymic.
State your first name and patronymic.

examples.text: Зови меня просто по имени, без отчества.
examples.trans: Call me simply by first name, without patronymic.
I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: a small quantity, couple of things

examples.text: Тогда положите мне ещё парочку блинов!
examples.trans: Then serve me a couple more pancakes!

examples.text: Это слово «парочка» часто звучит в разговоре.
examples.trans: This word 'couple' is often heard in conversation.

meanings.en: to put, to place, to lay down

examples.text: В гроб с собой икру не положишь!
examples.trans: You can't put caviar in your coffin to take with you!
Put the keys on the table.

examples.text: А вот сюда я её и положу! Отличный подарок будет!
examples.trans: Right here is where I will put it! It will be an excellent gift!

полюбить.gloss: to come to love, to grow fond of

meanings.en: to fall in love with, to grow fond of

examples.text: Я тебя полюбил. Ты мой друг.
examples.trans: I've grown fond of you. You're my friend.
She fell in love with this town right away.

examples.text: А кто полюбит меня, если растолстею?
examples.trans: And who will love me if I get fat?

examples.text: Знаете, Лев, я поправляюсь очень быстро.
examples.trans: You know, Lev, I gain weight very quickly.

examples.text: Это слово «поправляться» часто звучит в разговоре.
examples.trans: This word 'to gain weight' is often heard in conversation.

meanings.note: as a side word: Правда, всё нормально = Honestly, everything's fine
as a side word: Правда, всё нормально = Honestly, everything's fine

examples.text: Правда, Нин, всё нормально. Скажи что-нибудь, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Honestly, Nina, everything's fine. Say something, please.

meanings.note: Я прекрасно понимаю = I understand perfectly

examples.text: Нет, лучше так: все говорят, а я делаю! Прекрасно.
examples.trans: No, better like this: everyone talks, while I do! Excellent.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

растолстеть.gloss: to get fat; to put on weight

examples.text: А кто полюбит меня, если растолстею?
examples.trans: And who will love me if I get fat?

examples.text: Это слово «растолстеть» часто звучит в разговоре.
examples.trans: This word 'to get fat' is often heard in conversation.

meanings.note: у меня сердце = I have a bad heart (colloquial)

examples.text: Мне горько, мне плохо. У меня сердце.
examples.trans: I feel bitter, I feel awful. I have a bad heart.

examples.text: Я совсем не это хочу сказать.
examples.trans: That's not what I mean at all.

examples.text: Нет, Вика, я совсем не это хочу сказать.
examples.trans: No, Vika, that's not what I mean at all.

meanings.note: спасибо за + accusative = thank you for

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: at the start of a question

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

examples.text: Теперь я начальник нашей стройки. Ты уволен!
examples.trans: Now I'm the boss of our building site. You're fired!

examples.text: Я тебе тогда сказал: ты меня ещё поцелуешь.
examples.trans: I told you back then: you'll kiss me one day.

examples.text: Это слово «фигура» часто звучит в разговоре.
examples.trans: This word 'figure' is often heard in conversation.

meanings.note: the plural is a different word: люди, людям, о людях

examples.trans: There are a lot of people here.
I know the problems of ordinary people.

meanings.note: short form чисто: всё чисто = everything is clean

examples.text: Нин, я всё помыл. Всё чисто.
examples.trans: Nina, I washed everything. It's all clean.

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
